sections.heading: Before connecting a sender
sections.text:
Orbit 1.8 installations expose {{versions.1.8.api_prefix}}. These instructions describe that generation. Register a workspace before distributing its integration key. The key model is a {{legacy.v1_key_model}}; it does not offer the scope boundaries available in later clients. Keep a record of which sender owns each deployed copy. If several processes share a key, revoking it affects all of those processes.

Start with one device and one measurement series. Give the device a stable external identifier that survives an application restart. The display name belongs to the user interface and is not an integration key. A sender that changes the external identifier each time it boots creates a new identity instead of continuing the old history.

sections.heading: Retention and throughput
sections.text:
The provisioning default is {{versions.1.8.default_retention_days}} days of measurement retention. The workspace request budget is {{versions.1.8.rate_limit_per_minute}} requests per minute. Both values belong to the 1.8 contract; a dashboard exported from a newer installation is not a reliable description of this deployment.

A collection agent should retain its own outgoing queue until the server confirms acceptance. Do not delete the local sample solely because a TCP connection was opened. When a connection drops during a request, first determine whether the request was accepted. A network timeout does not prove that the server stored nothing. Record a stable sample identifier in the sender log to support reconciliation.

sections.heading: First handover
sections.text:
The 1.8 measurement notification is {{legacy.event_v1}}. Register the receiver against this event name rather than a name copied from a later release. Verify that the receiver can parse the payload before enabling a large device fleet. A callback acknowledges a submitted observation; it is not a replacement for the sender acceptance response.

The handover record should include the deployed version, workspace, device identifier and receiver owner. Do not include the workspace key. Keep a rollback copy of the sender configuration outside its running process. A successful request from one workstation is insufficient evidence that every deployed agent uses the same configuration.
